title: Rava bar Zimuna
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: What remains for us from him is his precious saying, which is stated in [Shabbat 112b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.112b.8): Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rava bar Zimuna: If the earlier ones were like angels, we are like human beings; and if the earlier ones were like human beings, we are like donkeys, etc.[^1]

The saying is repeated in [Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim, beginning of chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.5.1.6): Rabbi Abba Zemina, in the name of Rabbi Zeira: “If the earlier ones were angels,” etc.

In [Jerusalem Talmud Demai 1:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Demai.1.3.5), the reading is “Rabbi Abba bar Zavina (it should read Zemina) said in the name of Rabbi Zeira.” Hyman explains the difference by saying that he was the first Rabbi Zeira’s student and the second Rabbi Zeira’s teacher: in the Bavli, the second Rabbi Zeira reported in his name; in the Jerusalem Talmud, he reported in the first Rabbi Zeira’s name.[^2]

notes.text: The Bavli has Rabbi Zeira report Rava bar Zimuna. [Heilprin’s Rava bar Zemina headword](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3120&lang=en) redirects readers to Rabbi Abba.

Both linked Yerushalmi passages have Rabbi Abba bar Zemina report in Rabbi Zeira’s name. The linked Demai already reads Zemina, the form Hyman proposes in place of Zavina. His explanation invokes two Rabbi Zeiras.
